cards.name: mcx_and_tree_resynthesis
cards.identity: Recognize, by exact symbolic Boolean simulation of a Toffoli-level segment, that it implements a multi-controlled X: t ^= c1 & c2 & ... & ck (every other wire returns to its initial value, ancillas 0 -> 0). Discard the whole recognized segment and re-emit the same function as Gidney's temporary-logical-AND ladder/tree over k-1 CLEAN ancillas: b1 = and_compute(c1,c2); b2 = and_compute(b1,c3); ...; b_{k-1} = and_compute(b_{k-2},ck); cx(b_{k-1}, t); then and_uncompute(b_{k-1}), ..., and_uncompute(b1) in reverse order. Each and_compute is the 4-T |0>-initialized AND gadget (T,T,T,Tdg-style Toffoli-into-fresh-ancilla); each and_uncompute is H + Z-basis measurement on the ancilla with a classically controlled CZ fix-up on its two inputs, costing 0 T. A balanced binary tree (b = and_compute of pairs, then pairs of partial ANDs) is an equally valid emission with the same gadget count and lower depth; use the ladder when ancilla count is the tie-break, the tree when depth is.
cards.correctness: and_compute(x,y -> a) on a clean ancilla is the standard 4-T measurement-uncomputable AND: it maps |x>|y>|0> to |x>|y>|x&y> exactly (no relative phase after the Tdg correction in Gidney's gadget), so the ladder leaves b_{k-1} = c1&...&ck by induction (b1 = c1&c2; b_i = b_{i-1}&c_{i+1} = c1&...&c_{i+1}), and cx(b_{k-1}, t) sets t ^= AND(controls). and_uncompute measures the ancilla in the X basis after H; the outcome m is uniformly random and independent of the data, and conditioned on m the residual operator on the two input wires is CZ^m, which the classically controlled CZ cancels. Hence for every measurement branch m the branch Kraus operator is K_m |x> = c_m |f(x)> with c_m = 2^{-1/2} independent of x (phase consistency, invariant 2), and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1. Ancillas are returned to |0> (post-measurement reset by the classically controlled X on m, standard in the gadget). The function f is identical to the recognized segment's by construction, and recognition itself is exact: h-ccz-h on the target is ccx, so the segment is a classical reversible Toffoli network; propagating Boolean expressions (ancillas initialized to the constant 0) and canonicalizing them (BDD or sympy simplify_logic over the k+1 non-ancilla variables) decides wire-by-wire that the output map is exactly t ^= AND(c1..ck) with all other wires identity. No approximation: 0 charged to the error budget.
cards.trigger: A maximal segment of the op list containing only {ccz, ccx, cx, x, h} in which every h occurs as part of an h-ccz-h sandwich on one leg of a ccz (so the segment is equivalent to a pure ccx/cx/x network). Run symbolic Boolean simulation with ancilla wires (wires never read before first write, and written back to 0 at the end) set to constant 0 and all other wires set to free variables. Fire iff the canonicalized output assignment is: exactly one wire q_t has value v_t XOR (AND over a set S of >= 4 other wires), every wire in S is unchanged, and every remaining wire is unchanged (ancillas back to constant 0). The match records (q_t, S). On mcx_10 the whole 66-gate circuit is one such segment, giving q_t = the target and |S| = 10. Does not fire on adders/multipliers (their outputs are XOR-of-many-products, not a single full AND), and does not fire on segments with fewer than 4 controls (where the existing book rule is already optimal).
cards.expected_effect: All 32 ccz and all 34 h gates of mcx_10 disappear. They are replaced by 9 and_compute gadgets (4 T each = 36 T), 1 cx, and 9 zero-T measured and_uncomputes. The input is Barenco et al.'s 4(n-2) = 32-Toffoli borrowed-ancilla MCX, which pays 4 Toffolis per control because it must restore DIRTY ancillas; since the harness guarantees ancillas start in |0>, the restoration work is pure waste. T-count 128 -> 36 (below pyzx's 100 and TKET's 192). Qubit count 19 -> 20 (9 ancillas instead of 8); T is the first lexicographic key so this is a win, and the balanced-tree emission uses the same 9. On other reconstruction circuits in the suite the trigger does not fire, so no regression.
cards.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018), arXiv:1709.06648 (temporary logical-AND: 4 T to compute, 0 T measurement-based uncompute); the replaced structure is Barenco, Bennett, Cleve, DiVincenzo, Margolus, Shor, Sleator, Smolin, Weinfurter, PRA 52, 3457 (1995), Lemma 7.2 (4(n-2) Toffolis with borrowed ancillas); AND-ladder MCX cost 4n-4 T as in Jones, PRA 87, 022328 (2013) and Maslov, PRA 93, 022311 (2016).

cards.name: mcx_truthtable_recognition_and_ladder_resynthesis
cards.identity: Two-part rule. (1) RECOGNITION by complete truth-table simulation with bitmask arithmetic: a Toffoli-level segment of {ccz, ccx, cx, x, h} (h only as the h-ccz-h sandwich that makes a ccz into a ccx on that leg) over n <= 20 wires is a classical reversible network. Assign wire i the Boolean function 'input bit i' encoded as a single Python integer f_i of 2^n bits, where bit b of f_i is the value of wire i under the input assignment b (i.e. f_i = the fixed constant mask with bit b set iff b has bit i set; these are the standard n 'column masks' of an n-variable truth table). Simulate the gate list forward, updating only the written wire: x(a): f_a ^= FULL; cx(a,b): f_b ^= f_a; ccx(a,b,c): f_c ^= (f_a & f_b); cz/ccz on controls only after rewriting via the h-sandwich. No simplification, no sympy, no BDD -- every operation is one machine-word-parallel AND/XOR on a 2^n-bit integer, so the whole segment costs O(|gates| * 2^n / 64) word ops (for n = 19: 66 gates x 8 KiB = microseconds). Fire iff the final masks are: f_q == (column mask of q) for all q != t (every other wire exactly the identity function, including dirty ancilla wires, for ALL input values), and f_t == (column mask of t) XOR (AND over q in S of column mask of q) for exactly one wire t and a set S with |S| >= 4. The match records (t, S); emit at most ONE match per maximal segment and bail at the first mismatch, so the trigger is a single linear pass. (2) EMISSION: delete the whole recognized segment and rebuild t ^= AND(S) as Gidney's temporary-logical-AND ladder on k-1 = |S|-1 CLEAN ancillas: b1 = and_compute(s1, s2); b_i = and_compute(b_{i-1}, s_{i+1}) for i = 2..k-1; cx(b_{k-1}, t); then and_uncompute(b_{k-1}), ..., and_uncompute(b1) in reverse. and_compute is the 4-T clean-ancilla AND gadget; and_uncompute is H + Z-basis measurement with a classically controlled CZ fix-up on its two inputs, 0 T. Wires that the segment used as ancillas are provably untouched by the rest of the circuit's data flow only if they are not read elsewhere, so the emission does not reuse them: it requests k-1 fresh ancillas via ir_with_gates(..., n_qubits=n+extra), and the balanced-tree ordering is an equally valid emission with the same gadget count.
cards.correctness: Recognition is exact and complete, not heuristic: the 2^n-bit mask of a wire IS its full truth table over all n input wires, and the three update rules are exactly the Boolean semantics of x/cx/ccx. Equality of masks is therefore equality of functions on every one of the 2^n inputs, so firing certifies the segment's output map is precisely t -> t XOR AND(S) with every other wire (controls AND dirty-borrowed ancillas, for arbitrary ancilla input values) returned unchanged. This is why no ancilla-liveness analysis is needed and why the pathological cost of symbolic canonicalization disappears. Emission: and_compute(x,y -> a) maps |x>|y>|0> to |x>|y>|x&y> exactly with no relative phase, so by induction b1 = s1&s2 and b_i = b_{i-1}&s_{i+1} = s1&...&s_{i+1}, giving b_{k-1} = AND(S); cx(b_{k-1}, t) sets t ^= AND(S), matching the recognized function. and_uncompute measures the ancilla in the X basis; the outcome m is uniform and independent of the data, and conditioned on m the residual operator on the two input wires is CZ^m, cancelled by the classically controlled CZ. Hence for every branch m the Kraus operator is K_m|x> = c_m|f(x)> with c_m = 2^{-1/2} independent of x (phase consistency, invariant 2) and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1; ancillas end in |0> after the gadget's classically controlled X. Nothing is charged to the error budget.
cards.trigger: One maximal contiguous segment of the op list whose gates lie in {ccz, ccx, cx, x, h} with every h paired as h-ccz-h / h-ccx-h on a single leg (so the segment is a pure classical reversible ccx/cx/x network), with n <= 20 wires in the circuit (hard guard: if n > 20 the rule returns no match immediately, bounding the mask size at 2^20 bits = 128 KiB). Run the bitmask truth-table simulation above once over that segment; fire iff the output is exactly one wire t with f_t = col(t) XOR AND_{q in S} col(q), |S| >= 4, and f_q = col(q) for every other wire. Only the segment-level match is enumerated -- no subsegment search, no per-gate retriggering -- so the trigger is O(|gates| * 2^n / 64) with no symbolic algebra anywhere. On mcx_10 the whole 66-gate circuit is one such segment and the match is (t = the target wire, |S| = 10); on adders/multipliers the target wire's function is an XOR of several products, not a single full AND, so f_t never matches and the rule declines; it also declines for |S| < 4, where the existing and_ancilla_ccz_lowering book rule is already optimal.
cards.expected_effect: All 32 ccz and all 34 h gates of mcx_10 are deleted and replaced by 9 and_compute gadgets (4 T each = 36 T), 1 cx, and 9 zero-T measured and_uncomputes. The input is Barenco et al.'s 4(n-2) = 32-Toffoli DIRTY-ancilla MCX; since the harness guarantees clean |0> ancillas, the ancilla-restoration half of that construction is pure waste. T-count 128 -> 36 (below pyzx's 100, TKET's 192, BQSKit's 224). Qubits 19 -> 20 (9 fresh clean ancillas); T is the first lexicographic key, so the runner accepts. The previous attempt reached exactly this 36 T and was rejected only because its recognition used sympy simplify_logic / BDD canonicalization over the free variables, which blew the 300 s runtime budget; the bitmask truth table computes the same certificate in well under a second, which is the entire change.
cards.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018), arXiv:1709.06648 (temporary logical AND: 4 T to compute, 0 T measurement-based uncompute); replaced structure: Barenco, Bennett, Cleve, DiVincenzo, Margolus, Shor, Sleator, Smolin, Weinfurter, PRA 52, 3457 (1995), Lemma 7.2; AND-ladder MCX at 4k-4 T: Jones, PRA 87, 022328 (2013) and Maslov, PRA 93, 022311 (2016). Bitmask/word-parallel truth-table simulation of reversible networks: Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 4A, 7.1.3 (bitwise tricks / broadword computation).

cards.identity: Two-part rule. (1) RECOGNITION by complete truth-table simulation with bitmask arithmetic: a Toffoli-level segment of {ccz, ccx, cx, x, h} (h only as the h-ccz-h sandwich that makes a ccz into a ccx on that leg) over n <= 20 wires is a classical reversible network. Assign wire i the Boolean function 'input bit i' encoded as a single Python integer f_i of 2^n bits, where bit b of f_i is the value of wire i under the input assignment b (i.e. f_i = the fixed constant mask with bit b set iff b has bit i set; these are the standard n 'column masks' of an n-variable truth table). Simulate the gate list forward, updating only the written wire: x(a): f_a ^= FULL; cx(a,b): f_b ^= f_a; ccx(a,b,c): f_c ^= (f_a & f_b); cz/ccz on controls only after rewriting via the h-sandwich. No simplification, no sympy, no BDD -- every operation is one machine-word-parallel AND/XOR on a 2^n-bit integer, so the whole segment costs O(|gates| * 2^n / 64) word ops (for n = 19: 66 gates x 8 KiB = microseconds). Fire iff the final masks are: f_q == (column mask of q) for all q != t (every other wire exactly the identity function, including dirty ancilla wires, for ALL input values), and f_t == (column mask of t) XOR (AND over q in S of column mask of q) for exactly one wire t and a set S with |S| >= 4. The match records (t, S); emit at most ONE match per maximal segment and bail at the first mismatch, so the trigger is a single linear pass. (2) EMISSION: delete the whole recognized segment and rebuild t ^= AND(S) as Gidney's temporary-logical-AND ladder on k-1 = |S|-1 CLEAN ancillas: b1 = and_compute(s1, s2); b_i = and_compute(b_{i-1}, s_{i+1}) for i = 2..k-1; cx(b_{k-1}, t); then and_uncompute(b_{k-1}), ..., and_uncompute(b1) in reverse. and_compute is the 4-T clean-ancilla AND gadget; and_uncompute is H + Z-basis measurement with a classically controlled CZ fix-up on its two inputs, 0 T. Wires that the segment used as ancillas are provably untouched by the rest of the circuit's data flow only if they are not read elsewhere, so the emission does not reuse them: it requests k-1 fresh ancillas via ir_with_gates(..., n_qubits=n+extra), and the balanced-tree ordering is an equally valid emission with the same gadget count.
cards.correctness: Recognition is exact and complete, not heuristic: the 2^n-bit mask of a wire IS its full truth table over all n input wires, and the three update rules are exactly the Boolean semantics of x/cx/ccx. Equality of masks is therefore equality of functions on every one of the 2^n inputs, so firing certifies the segment's output map is precisely t -> t XOR AND(S) with every other wire (controls AND dirty-borrowed ancillas, for arbitrary ancilla input values) returned unchanged. This is why no ancilla-liveness analysis is needed and why the pathological cost of symbolic canonicalization disappears. Emission: and_compute(x,y -> a) maps |x>|y>|0> to |x>|y>|x&y> exactly with no relative phase, so by induction b1 = s1&s2 and b_i = b_{i-1}&s_{i+1} = s1&...&s_{i+1}, giving b_{k-1} = AND(S); cx(b_{k-1}, t) sets t ^= AND(S), matching the recognized function. and_uncompute measures the ancilla in the X basis; the outcome m is uniform and independent of the data, and conditioned on m the residual operator on the two input wires is CZ^m, cancelled by the classically controlled CZ. Hence for every branch m the Kraus operator is K_m|x> = c_m|f(x)> with c_m = 2^{-1/2} independent of x (phase consistency, invariant 2) and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1; ancillas end in |0> after the gadget's classically controlled X. Nothing is charged to the error budget.
cards.trigger: One maximal contiguous segment of the op list whose gates lie in {ccz, ccx, cx, x, h} with every h paired as h-ccz-h / h-ccx-h on a single leg (so the segment is a pure classical reversible ccx/cx/x network), with n <= 20 wires in the circuit (hard guard: if n > 20 the rule returns no match immediately, bounding the mask size at 2^20 bits = 128 KiB). Run the bitmask truth-table simulation above once over that segment; fire iff the output is exactly one wire t with f_t = col(t) XOR AND_{q in S} col(q), |S| >= 4, and f_q = col(q) for every other wire. Only the segment-level match is enumerated -- no subsegment search, no per-gate retriggering -- so the trigger is O(|gates| * 2^n / 64) with no symbolic algebra anywhere. On mcx_10 the whole 66-gate circuit is one such segment and the match is (t = the target wire, |S| = 10); on adders/multipliers the target wire's function is an XOR of several products, not a single full AND, so f_t never matches and the rule declines; it also declines for |S| < 4, where the existing and_ancilla_ccz_lowering book rule is already optimal.
cards.expected_effect: All 32 ccz and all 34 h gates of mcx_10 are deleted and replaced by 9 and_compute gadgets (4 T each = 36 T), 1 cx, and 9 zero-T measured and_uncomputes. The input is Barenco et al.'s 4(n-2) = 32-Toffoli DIRTY-ancilla MCX; since the harness guarantees clean |0> ancillas, the ancilla-restoration half of that construction is pure waste. T-count 128 -> 36 (below pyzx's 100, TKET's 192, BQSKit's 224). Qubits 19 -> 20 (9 fresh clean ancillas); T is the first lexicographic key, so the runner accepts. The previous attempt reached exactly this 36 T and was rejected only because its recognition used sympy simplify_logic / BDD canonicalization over the free variables, which blew the 300 s runtime budget; the bitmask truth table computes the same certificate in well under a second, which is the entire change.
cards.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018), arXiv:1709.06648 (temporary logical AND: 4 T to compute, 0 T measurement-based uncompute); replaced structure: Barenco, Bennett, Cleve, DiVincenzo, Margolus, Shor, Sleator, Smolin, Weinfurter, PRA 52, 3457 (1995), Lemma 7.2; AND-ladder MCX at 4k-4 T: Jones, PRA 87, 022328 (2013) and Maslov, PRA 93, 022311 (2016). Bitmask/word-parallel truth-table simulation of reversible networks: Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 4A, 7.1.3 (bitwise tricks / broadword computation).
